title: Open WebUI URL ingest -- T1190 NAT64-wrapped IPv4 bypasses is_global SSRF filter
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70485 (GHSA-8x5v-cpv7-8jjp,
CVSS 7.1 HIGH), affecting Open WebUI from 0.9.0 until 0.11.0.

Open WebUI checked whether a user-supplied URL destination was globally
routable by applying Python's `ipaddress.is_global` to the LITERAL
IPv6 address -- without examining IPv4 addresses embedded inside IPv6
TRANSITION encodings. On a deployment with a NAT64 gateway (common in
IPv6-only or dual-stack-with-NAT64 setups, including some Kubernetes
clusters), any verified user can wrap an internal or cloud-metadata
IPv4 address inside the NAT64 well-known prefix (`64:ff9b::/96`); the
wrapped address passes `is_global` as a seemingly-ordinary global IPv6
literal, but the NAT64 gateway unwraps it back to the internal IPv4
target at connection time -- reaching it through RAG URL ingestion,
URL-to-markdown conversion, or web-search content retrieval, with the
internal response body returned to the requesting user.

This corpus already carries a Pydantic AI rule for a structurally
identical class of bug (`CVE-2026-46678`/`CVE-2026-48782`-style IPv6
transition-encoding blocklist bypass is NOT yet in this corpus, but the
underlying pattern -- checking the wrapper form instead of the
unwrapped target -- recurs across multiple SSRF-protection
implementations); this rule is Open WebUI's own specific instance.

Detection logic flags a URL-ingestion request whose target hostname is
an IPv6 literal within the NAT64 well-known prefix
(`64:ff9b::/96`) -- a legitimate public URL has no reason to be
expressed in NAT64-wrapped form rather than a plain IPv4/IPv6 address
or hostname.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact fix commit), fixed in 0.11.0.
